entries.name: Radio Engineering Handbook
entries.description: A beginner's course in how radio works, from electromagnetic waves to your first station. 90 chapters, written in order, but each one stands alone.
entries.licenseNote: Written by Tyler Allen for LogBook73 and included under its MIT licence. It is a beginner's course, not an official text and not legal advice. LogBook73 gives it no review date; its chapters were last changed there on 2026-11-03, and Outpost has not checked them against other sources.

entries.description: A budget multi-band handheld with VHF/UHF transmit, wideband SSB/shortwave receive, GPS and APRS. The factory manual is nine pages and explains almost nothing. This is the guide it should have shipped with: the documented menu system decoded, the theory behind each setting, ready-made configurations, and the APRS know-how the radio assumes you already have.
